topics.label: Introduction and Course Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This topic introduces the cancer biology lecture series, student cohorts, and the primary learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Cancer as a Disruption of Cellular Differentiation and Tissue Architecture
topics.groupedBecause: They establish how cancer develops through cumulative genetic and epigenetic alterations that break down normal multicellular differentiation and tissue architecture.

topics.label: Invasion, Metastasis, and Tumor Progression
topics.groupedBecause: They explain the histological and clinical distinctions between benign lesions and invasive, metastasizing malignancies, using the adenoma-carcinoma sequence as a prime example.

topics.label: Tumor Nomenclature and Classification
topics.groupedBecause: This topic outlines the standardized naming conventions and exceptions used to classify tumors based on their tissue origin and malignancy status.

topics.label: Pathophysiological Mechanisms of Cancer Morbidity and Mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This topic details the anatomical, functional, and systemic mechanisms by which primary and metastatic tumors cause illness and death in patients.

topics.label: Cancer Incidence Across Tissues and Animal Species
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the prevalence and tissue distribution of tumors in human populations and across diverse multicellular animal taxa.

topics.label: Principles and Clinical Application of Cancer Screening
topics.groupedBecause: They explore the rationale, diagnostic methods, and comparative efficacy of screening programs for early cancer detection across different organ systems.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Practical Briefing
topics.groupedBecause: This topic concludes the lecture with a reminder of the learning outcomes and instructions for upcoming practical sessions.
